robot.name: RobotEra L7
robot.status_notes: China Daily reported official launch on 2025-07-29 with 200 robots shipped company-wide in 2025, but MERA Robotics lists L7 as in development and not selling openly yet. No public price, named L7 customer deployment, or proven autonomy was found.

height.notes: Source 1 and 3 state 171 cm; Source 4 datasheet lists 1.71 m.

weight.notes: TechEBlog says 65 kg; MERA Robotics says 65 kg without hands. Source 1 does not list weight.

payload.notes: Source 1 says 20 kg double-arm load; Source 4 specifies with elbows bent 90° the two arms hold 20 kg together.

runtime.notes: No runtime rating found in reviewed sources.

battery.notes: MERA Robotics lists battery capacity as 60 V 15 Ah based on Robotera datasheet; capacity in Wh not specified directly.

degrees_of_freedom.notes: Full-body DoF includes 31 body DoF plus 12 per hand = 55; Source 3 says 55 total with each arm 7 and hands 12.

walking_speed.notes: All sources list 4 m/s running speed; walking speed not published.

hands.description: XHAND1 dexterous hands with 12 active directly driven DoF per hand; five-finger.

compute.description: 80 TOPS (x86) plus 275 TOPS (NVIDIA Orin) according to MERA Robotics catalog.

actuators.description: In-house knee joints peak at 400 N·m and 25 rad/s according to MERA Robotics catalog.

availability.notes: No official price published; MERA Robotics says status in development and not selling openly yet; inquiries go to sales team.

manipulation_dexterity.summary: L7 has XHAND1 12-DoF hands and 20 kg double-arm load. Demos described in media show sword dancing with mid-motion grip changes, screw-driving, tearing paper towels, pulling curtains, and a massage at CES 2026.
caveats: No success rates or repeatability data.
Sword dance is observed via media description, not independent video review.
YouTube titles only; no transcript confirms massage details beyond title.

autonomy_task_execution.summary: ERA-42 VLA model is claimed to drive full-body control. Founder describes hybrid training with teleoperation data. No demo explicitly states autonomous execution; teleoperation_status is not_disclosed for all reviewed L7 demos.
caveats: No autonomy statement in any L7 demo video or article.
Teleoperation use for data generation is confirmed by founder but not for real-time demos.
No independent autonomy benchmark.

mobility_whole_body_control.summary: 171 cm, 65 kg robot performs 360-degree spins, breakdancing, sword dance with leaps, flips, and stable landings; listed running speed 4 m/s.
caveats: No fall-rate or disturbance recovery data.
Media descriptions and video titles only; not independently verified.

perception_scene_understanding.summary: Binocular vision, 3D LiDAR with 360° FOV, stereo camera, microphones; ERA-42 fuses perception with generative capabilities.
caveats: No perception benchmark or real-world task evidence shown.
Hardware spec claims from directory, not official product page.

human_interaction.summary: Speaker and microphone listed; massage demo at CES 2026 indicated by video title only.
caveats: No demonstrated conversation or instruction-following.
Massage claim is only a video title, no transcript.

endurance_reliability.summary: Company reports 200 robots shipped across products in 2025 and hundreds more in production; however no runtime, MTBF, or reliability test specific to L7.
caveats: Shipment figures are company-wide, not L7-specific.
No independent audit of deliveries or reliability.

human_environment_fit.summary: Human-sized height 171 cm, weight 65 kg, titanium/carbon fiber build; intended for logistics, industrial, and service roles.
caveats: No safety certification found.
Weight is 65 kg without hands per datasheet; actual total may differ.

deployment_commercial_proof.summary: No named L7 customer deployment found. Company claims nine of top ten most valuable tech companies as customers, but not necessarily for L7; MERA datasheet names no L7 customers.
caveats: Commercial claims are company-level, not L7-specific.
No units, hours, or output metrics for L7.

accessibility_value.summary: No official price or public purchase path. MERA Robotics lists status as in development and not selling openly yet; inquiries go to sales team.
caveats: Not openly purchasable as of review date.
Reseller estimates vary but no official price.

evidence_items.title: Robot Era L7 product listing
evidence_items.claim: L7 is a bipedal humanoid robot using the ERA-42 VLA model to drive full-body 55 degrees of freedom, with 20 kg double-arm load, 4 m/s running speed, 12-DoF dexterous hand, and 360-degree perception.
evidence_items.notes: Directory listing, not official product page; specs appear to be from manufacturer.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Robot Era’s L7 bipedal humanoid robot is a Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model.
evidence_items.source_location: Humanoid Robotics Technology product page, description section
evidence_items.verification_notes: No independent measurement; source is a directory, not the manufacturer.

evidence_items.title: L7 sensor suite
evidence_items.claim: L7 is equipped with binocular vision and 3D LiDAR, offering a 360° field of view and full-area perception.
evidence_items.notes: Directory listing; sensor claim not independently verified.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Equipped with binocular vision and 3D LiDAR, the system offers complex environmental adaptability, a 360° field of view, and full-area perception.
evidence_items.source_location: Humanoid Robotics Technology product page, description section

evidence_items.title: ERA-42 VLA model development
evidence_items.claim: Robot Era has developed ERA-42, a vision-language-action model that fuses perception with generative capabilities.
evidence_items.notes: Founder interview in reputable media; not a formal company press release.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: On the software side, Robot Era has developed ERA-42, a vision-language-action (VLA) model that fuses perception with generative capabilities.
evidence_items.verification_notes: No technical paper or benchmark linked in article.

evidence_items.title: Teleoperation data generation
evidence_items.claim: Robot Era uses a hybrid approach starting with massive video datasets, then fine-tunes using high-quality teleoperation data.
evidence_items.notes: Founder statement; does not address whether L7 demos are teleoperated.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Indicates teleoperation involved in training, not necessarily deployment.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: We start with massive video datasets to pretrain generalist models, then fine-tune using high-quality teleoperation data.
evidence_items.source_location: KrASIA article, interview answer about teleoperation
evidence_items.verification_notes: Teleoperation for data collection is disclosed, but teleoperation_status of demos is not.

evidence_items.title: L7 physical specifications
evidence_items.claim: L7 is 171 cm tall, 65 kg, built with titanium and carbon fiber, with 55 degrees of freedom, each arm 7 DoF, and hands with 12 DoF between them.
evidence_items.notes: Media report likely based on company specs; weight may exclude hands according to MERA.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: The L7 is a 171 cm tall, 65 kg robot with a lightweight build constructed of titanium and carbon fiber, complete with tons of flexibility.
evidence_items.verification_notes: No direct measurement; conflict with MERA's '65 kg without hands' noted.

evidence_items.title: Sword dance performance
evidence_items.claim: L7 performed a sword dance with leaps, flips, precise sword control, mid-motion grip changes, and stable landings without wobbles or stumbles.
evidence_items.notes: Descriptive media account of a video; not independently reviewed.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Strong observable whole-body control and dexterity, but no autonomy claim.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Jumps land cleanly, with no wobbles or stumbles, as it accelerates and increases until it comes to a rest with the sword extended.
evidence_items.source_location: TechEBlog article, sword dance performance description
evidence_items.verification_notes: Teleoperation_status not disclosed; article does not state autonomous.

evidence_items.title: MERA Robotics detailed specs
evidence_items.claim: L7 datasheet lists 1.71 m height, 65 kg without hands, 31 body DoF, 55 including XHAND1 hands, each arm 7 DoF, 20 kg payload, knee joints peak 400 N·m and 25 rad/s.
evidence_items.notes: Directory entry based on Robotera datasheet, but not the official datasheet itself.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Detailed specs for comparison, but lower confidence due to indirect source.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: The datasheet lists 1.71 m height and 65 kg without hands.
evidence_items.source_location: MERA Robotics catalogue, Robotera L7 design and technology section
evidence_items.verification_notes: Conflicts with TechEBlog's 65 kg (implied with hands); directory not manufacturer.

evidence_items.title: Battery and compute specs
evidence_items.claim: Battery capacity is listed as 60 V, 15 Ah, compute as 80 TOPS (x86) plus 275 TOPS (NVIDIA Orin).
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Battery capacity is listed as 60 V, 15 Ah, and compute as 80 TOPS (x86) plus 275 TOPS (NVIDIA Orin).
evidence_items.source_location: MERA Robotics catalogue, Robotera L7 design section
evidence_items.verification_notes: No runtime extrapolation possible without official data.

evidence_items.title: Availability status
evidence_items.claim: L7 is in development and not selling openly yet; manufacturer has shown the robot but no open sale.
evidence_items.notes: Directory status; consistent with no price found.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Status: In development: the manufacturer has shown the robot but is not selling it openly yet.
evidence_items.verification_notes: No purchase path or price available.

evidence_items.title: Official launch of ROBOTERA L7
evidence_items.claim: Robotera officially launched L7, a full-sized bipedal humanoid capable of high-dynamic movement and fine manipulation.
evidence_items.notes: China Daily state media; reports company statements.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Chinese robotics startup Robotera, backed by Tsinghua University, has officially launched its next-generation full-sized humanoid robot, the ROBOTERA L7.
evidence_items.verification_notes: Launch does not imply public sale.

evidence_items.title: L7 demonstrated capabilities
evidence_items.claim: L7 can perform 360-degree spins, breakdancing, sorting, scanning, screw-driving, tearing paper towels, and pulling curtains.
evidence_items.notes: Media description of demos; teleoperation not mentioned.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Broad capability set, but no autonomy confirmation.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Showcasing a wide range of capabilities, the L7 can perform high-dynamic maneuvers like explosive 360-degree spins and breakdancing moves, while also handling practical industrial functions such as sorting, scanning, and screw-driving in logistics and factory settings.
evidence_items.verification_notes: No autonomous statement; demos may be scripted or teleoperated.

evidence_items.title: Company commercial claims
evidence_items.claim: Robotera has shipped 200 humanoid robots in 2025, with over one hundred orders in progress and nine of top ten most valuable tech companies as customers.
evidence_items.notes: Company-wide figures, not specific to L7.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Shows company traction, not L7 deployment.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Highlighting the company's rapid commercial growth fueled by its technological advancements, Robotera revealed that, so far it has shipped 200 humanoid robots shipped in 2025, with over one hundred orders currently in progress.
evidence_items.source_location: China Daily article, commercial growth section
evidence_items.verification_notes: No independent audit; may include other models like XHand, Q5, STAR1.

evidence_items.title: Missing disclosures
evidence_items.claim: No runtime, walking speed, autonomy confirmation, price, or named L7 customer deployment was found in reviewed sources.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Judges should reduce confidence on autonomy, endurance, and value.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Gaps identified across all reviewed primary and secondary sources.
evidence_items.verification_notes: Absence of disclosure, not evidence of inability.

researcher_notes.short_verdict_for_arena: RobotEra L7 shows impressive mobility (sword dance, 360-degree spins, breakdancing) and fine manipulation (screw-driving, paper tearing, massage) in media-described demos, but no autonomy confirmation, no price, no runtime, and no named L7 customer deployment. Treat as a prototype with strong kinematic demos but unproven autonomy and commercial readiness.

arena_prompt_summary.one_paragraph_summary: RobotEra L7 is a 171 cm, 65 kg full-size bipedal humanoid with 55 DoF and XHAND1 12-DoF hands, claimed to run the ERA-42 VLA model. It has demonstrated impressive whole-body mobility in media-described videos: 360-degree spins, breakdancing, and a sword dance with leaps and stable landings, plus fine manipulation such as screw-driving, paper towel tearing, and a CES 2026 massage title. However, no L7 demo discloses autonomy, no price or runtime is published, and no named L7 customer deployment exists. Commercial claims of 200 robots shipped are company-wide. Overall, strong kinematic demos but unproven autonomy and accessibility.
